title: Real Madrid, Liverpool and PSG Circle Ferran Torres After World Cup Final Heroics
excerpt: Barcelona's World Cup hero faces a transfer tug-of-war as three European giants jostle for his signature, with the Catalan club yet to offer him a new contract.
body:
• L'Equipe reports Real Madrid, Liverpool and PSG have all expressed interest in Barcelona forward Ferran Torres, 26, whose contract expires in June 2027.
  • Torres scored the winning goal in Spain's 1-0 extra-time victory over Argentina in the 2026 FIFA World Cup final, sharply raising his market value.
  • Barcelona plan to hold a decisive meeting with Torres' camp next week but have no renewal offer on the table, leaving the door open for rival clubs.
  • Aston Villa have reportedly tabled a €50 million bid, while Real Madrid view Torres as a fallback option if their pursuit of Bayern Munich's Michael Olise stalls.

Three Clubs, One World Cup Hero

Ferran Torres has gone from dependable squad player to the most talked-about forward in European football in the space of 120 minutes. The 26-year-old's extra-time strike that sealed Spain's 1-0 victory over Argentina in the 2026 FIFA World Cup final has triggered a scramble among some of the continent's biggest clubs.

According to L'Equipe journalist Tanzi Loïc, Liverpool and Paris Saint-Germain are both interested in signing Torres this summer. Hours later, the same outlet reported that arch-rivals Real Madrid have quietly added the Barcelona attacker to their shortlist as they search for a right-sided winger.

"I don't know and I don't care right now. Tomorrow is the important thing."

— Ferran Torres, speaking before Spain's World Cup opener against Cape Verde

Barcelona's Contract Dilemma

Barcelona signed Torres from Manchester City in January 2022 for €55 million. He has since scored 65 goals and provided 23 assists in 207 appearances across all competitions, including 21 goals in 49 games during the 2025-26 season under Hansi Flick.

Those are solid, if not superstar, numbers. But with his contract running until June 2027, the clock is ticking. If no deal is struck this summer, Torres can negotiate with overseas clubs from January and leave for free next year. Barcelona want to avoid another departure without a transfer fee.

Sporting director Deco and president Joan Laporta have made Torres' situation a priority, according to Mundo Deportivo. A meeting with the player's representatives is expected next week, once the post-World Cup break concludes. However, Financial Fair Play constraints had previously pushed Barcelona's renewal timeline to September, a delay that now looks increasingly risky given the rising interest.

Who Wants What

PSG have led the pursuit longest. Coach Luis Enrique, who managed Torres during his stint as Spain head coach, is keen on a reunion and values the forward's tactical versatility. Reports from Soccerway indicate Barcelona are demanding at least €50 million, a figure PSG can afford but have been cautious about meeting for a player in his final contract year.

Liverpool's interest, reported via Get French Football News, fits their summer strategy. Manager Andoni Iraola has already added Spain's Victor Muñoz from Osasuna and is looking for another forward who can operate across the front line. Torres' Premier League experience from his time at Manchester City gives him an edge over other options, and his 21-goal season suggests reliable output rather than a speculative gamble.

Real Madrid's entry is the most provocative. Signing a player directly from Barcelona carries enormous political weight in Spanish football. According to L'Equipe, Los Blancos view Torres as an alternative to Michael Olise, whose transfer from Bayern Munich has stalled over fee and personal terms. New manager Jose Mourinho is primarily seeking midfield and defensive reinforcements, but an unsettled Vinicius Jr. contract situation could yet open a forward slot.

Adding further heat, El Nacional reports that Aston Villa have tabled a €50 million offer, making this a four-way contest.

What It Means for Indian Football Fans

Torres' potential move to the Premier League would add another high-profile name for Indian viewers who have driven record viewership numbers for the league across the subcontinent. Liverpool and Real Madrid rank among the most followed clubs in India, and the transfer window drama around a World Cup final hero is the kind of storyline that cuts through to casual fans and fantasy league participants alike.

What Comes Next

The next seven to ten days are decisive. Barcelona's meeting with Torres' representatives will clarify whether a renewal is realistic or whether the club pivots to extracting a maximum fee. If talks collapse, expect PSG, Liverpool and potentially Real Madrid to move quickly before the August transfer deadline. Torres himself has remained tight-lipped, telling reporters before the World Cup that he was "not interested" in discussing speculation — though his stock has risen sharply since then.
